name: Bryce Rambach
summary: One custom ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.1, 1), carries almost everything from 0.3s to 1.3s. Cards lift out of their berths and sink back on an ease-in, letters rise, and a small overshoot marks the nav.

tiers.label: project card lifting out of its berth
card sinking back into its berth

honestyNote: Eleven canvases draw with 2D contexts (no WebGL); whatever they animate isn't in these numbers. Scripts asked matchMedia about reduced motion 6,137 times in one visit, which looks like a check on every animation frame.
notes: A dedicated ease-in exit: the card rises in 1.15s on ease-out and drops in 0.6s on cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.75, 0.25).
Reduced motion stops everything the tool could see: 293 timed events became 0.
The live build differs from the Oak and Clay build the notes measured; both are listed, with dates.

fromNotes.label: Oak and Clay statement (Settle, via Motion)
fromNotes.text: Measured from source (main @ 3512894), not the browser: the earlier build drove its statement tier from JavaScript, once per element, 0.65s to 1.1s. The live site on 2026-10-17 is the later sky build, on cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.1, 1) at 0.9s to 1.3s.

fromNotes.label: Oak and Clay signature (--ease-stamp)
fromNotes.text: At 0.3s, 0.45s and 0.5s. It became the house signature tier. Live: the overshoot habit survives as cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.5, 0.64, 1) on the nav marker.

fromNotes.label: Oak and Clay ambient loops
fromNotes.text: 14 keyframe sets at 2.6s to 21s, named after behaviour (hare-breath, ear-hello). Live: 12 looping elements, all sky-drift and sky-swell.

fromNotes.label: Oak and Clay reduced motion
fromNotes.text: Three layers: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user", useReducedMotion in seven components, and a CSS backstop. Live: 121 movement events became 0.
